[!] THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE E9 READER-ORPHAN PATTERN AND AGAIN IT WAS FOUND BY SOMETHING FAILING LOUDLY, NOT BY THE SWEEP. It bites EVERY Tier-1 self-landing PR from here on, so the population is 'all future lanes', not one branch. [!] DO NOT fix it by weakening R13 -- it fails closed on purpose and the loss it guards is real. Fix the REMEDY TEXT and the ordering so the per-branch route is named first, and decide explicitly whether the shared-board fallback should be removed now that its register is archived. · next: `dispatch_lane` · rerun: `git checkout -B tmp/pi-0002-probe origin/main && printf '{"tier":1,"landing":"self","why":"probe"}' > .github/pr-landing/tmp-pi-0002-probe.json && touch .github/pr-automerge-requests/tmp-pi-0002-probe.txt && git add -A && git commit -qm probe && python3 scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py --base origin/main; # FINDING STILL APPLIES if the failure text names docs/claude/session-board.json before scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py`
- **PI-20260921-0003** [routed → `E9 (session_01JVPxS3XjMyiN3J3HpQPkNq) -- same reader-orphan class, same sweep; E9 is already scoped to every consumer of an archived path anywhere`] THE GUARD THAT ENFORCES 'THE MANAGER MAY NOT TAKE AN ITEM' IS NOW STRUCTURALLY BLIND, AND IT FAILS OPEN. scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py derives WHO THE MANAGER IS from the git history of docs/claude/work/MANAGER-LEASE.json -- deliberately, and its docstring argues at length why branch-name and register-authorship were both rejected as identifiers. The 2026-09-21 reset ARCHIVED that lease file. Measured 2026-09-21 on branch claude/metis-insights-manager-9qmm63 with four manager commits in the range: the guard returned 'manager-scope: no_manager_commits ... 0 manager commit(s) in 4 commit(s) graded', exit 0. [!] THE EXIT CODE IS THE PROBLEM. A guard that cannot identify its subject reports GREEN, so 'no violation' and 'could not look' are collapsed into one value -- the exact class scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py exists to prevent, in a guard whose own docstring says an unrecognised value 'must not arm anything'. [!] .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md BOTH still state this rule is CI-enforced by this script. That claim is now false, and a false claim of enforcement is worse than a stated absence: this repo's record is that the prose rule alone was read and disobeyed THREE TIMES, which is why the mechanism was built. [!] The lease is NOT to be resurrected -- the reset retired it deliberately. So the real question is what identifies the manager under the new operating model, where the manager's register is MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json and lanes are spawned as sessions with recorded ids. The `lane` field on a checklist row is a candidate identifier that did not exist when this guard was written. · next: `dispatch_lane` · rerun: `python3 scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py; # FINDING STILL APPLIES while the output reads `no_manager_commits` on a branch whose commits carry a manager session's Claude-Session trailer, or while the lease-holder roster is derived from an archived file`
- **PI-20260921-0004** [routed → `THE OPERATOR, via section 2 of the next daily brief -- because the durable half of this fix CANNOT be delegated. [!] MEASURED 2026-09-21: the manager attempted to spawn a lane to write the spawn recipe into .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md and the create_session call was REFUSED by the auto-mode permission classifier, reason `[Self-Modification]` -- an agent spawning another agent to rewrite its own operating instructions. That refusal is CORRECT and was not worked around. [!] SO THE ITEM SPLITS, and the halves have different owners. (a) THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF IS ALREADY APPLIED and needs nobody: the manager now passes append_system_prompt carrying provenance plus the in-repo artifacts that let a lane VERIFY rather than trust, and now reads status_bucket + post_turn_summary after every dispatch rather than treating `idle` as finished. (b) THE DURABLE HALF -- writing that recipe into the manager contract so the NEXT manager inherits it -- needs either the operator to make the edit, or an explicit operator grant for a lane to write under .claude/skills/. [!] UNTIL (b) LANDS THIS FIX DIES WITH THIS SESSION, which is precisely the class of loss the operator named as the number-one failure mode. That is the decision being put to them, and it is one line either way.`] SPAWNED LANES STALL ON AN AUTHENTICITY CHECK, AND THE MANAGER CANNOT ANSWER THEM. Measured 2026-09-21 on the first six-lane dispatch under the new operating model: THREE of six lanes (A3a session_01AR9SV7kwUg8YBq38UVuVSN, A1 session_012LibLs7RYy22hCFWqohV2P, and the PI-20260921-0001 lane session_01W7iGwkrozCQ8LYRSM8WgGE) ended their FIRST turn without doing any work, each asking whether its own task prompt was legitimate or injected. The cause is structural, not a model quirk: a session created via create_session receives the manager's dispatch with NO human turn in the conversation, and a task that says 'edit infra and open a PR' arriving with no visible human sender is exactly what a session is supposed to be suspicious of. The lanes were RIGHT to ask. [!] THE MANAGER HAS NO DIRECT REPLY CHANNEL. There is no send_message tool in the manager's toolset and ListAgents does not list cloud sessions, so the only working path found was create_trigger(persistent_session_id=<lane>) followed by fire_trigger -- which DID deliver and unblocked two of the three. The third was refused by the auto-mode permission classifier, correctly, because that lane was sitting on a pending AskUserQuestion and firing into it would have answered a permission prompt on the operator's behalf. So one lane stays blocked until a human clicks. [!] THE COST IS NOT THE FIX-UP, IT IS THE SILENCE: a stalled lane reads as `idle` in list_sessions, which is what a FINISHED lane also reads as. A manager that did not inspect status_bucket and post_turn_summary would have recorded six lanes dispatched and come back to three that never started. [!] THE LIKELY FIX is create_session's `append_system_prompt`, which puts provenance where a lane reads it before its first tool call, plus naming the in-repo artifacts that CORROBORATE the dispatch (the checklist row, the pipeline item whose routed_to names the lane's own session id) so the lane can verify rather than trust. Confirming a suspicious instruction by asserting harder is not the answer; pointing at independently checkable evidence is. [!] REPLY-CHANNEL MECHANICS, MEASURED 2026-09-21 so the next manager does not re-derive them at a lane's expense. create_trigger(persistent_session_id=<lane>) then fire_trigger(trigger_id) with NO other argument delivers into that lane (confirmed: the result's session_id came back as cse_<same suffix as the lane>). Passing fire_trigger's optional `text` argument does NOT do that -- it SPAWNED A FRESH SESSION instead (session_016iHXA8iHzCaJkcmxU32ALR, titled '# unblock A1', origin force_run_trigger, no repo sources, $0.18 burned doing nothing; archived). So: fire bare. [!] AND THE SAME CALL IS REFUSED, CORRECTLY, when the target lane holds a pending permission prompt -- firing into it would answer that prompt on the operator's behalf. That refusal is a boundary to respect, not a bug to route around; such a lane stays blocked until a human clicks, and the manager's job is to SURFACE it, not to clear it. · next: `ask_operator` · rerun: `# Spawn one lane via create_session with a build-task prompt and NO append_system_prompt, then read its status_bucket and post_turn_summary from list_sessions after its first turn. FINDING STILL APPLIES if status_category is 'need_input' with a question about the task's legitimacy rather than about the task itself.`
